name: H World
headline: China's largest hotel franchisor, collecting fees while franchisees put up the buildings.
what_short: Hotel franchisor and operator, mostly in China
what_it_does: H World franchises and runs hotels. At the end of 2025 it had 12,858 hotels with 1.26 million rooms in 1,222 cities, almost all in greater China. Only 4.5% of the hotels are leased or owned by the company. The rest are franchised, and the owners pay it an upfront fee plus a monthly fee of about 3% to 6.5% of each hotel's revenue.
why_it_passed: Franchisees pay for developing and running their hotels, so the fee business needs very little of the company's own money.
Cash produced in 2025 was RMB 7.06 billion on about RMB 7.8 billion of tangible operating assets, a return of the order of 90%.
Its main Chinese hotel business carried the group: about RMB 23.9 billion of adjusted operating profit over 2021 to 2025, while the European business lost money.
Its loyalty program and direct booking channels keep hotels and guests inside its system.
why_not_now: At $44.17 per ADS (a share certificate traded in the US) the price sits inside the analysis's value range of $37.59 to $91.53, but even the central growth case earns only about 4.2% a year. That is well short of the roughly 10% the framework requires, and the analysis's fair price is $14.08.
watch: The European business (leased hotels in Germany) had negative operating profit in three of five years, and its brand was written down RMB 391 million in 2024.
Leases are a large commitment: RMB 27 billion of lease liabilities, with rent equal to 16.5% of revenue in 2025.
It has bought back its own shares at about $44.4 per ADS, well above the analysis's fair price.
The value depends heavily on which years are treated as normal: counting the post-COVID recovery would move the fair price from $14 to about $38.
